rationale: Evidence (iteration 1, 60 trials): the oval finishes 20/20 at 1.97 s with rms 0.005 m, so the lower kp and higher kd stabilised the controller. The s-bend finishes 12/20 and goes off track in the other 8, and the slalom finishes 0/20 with progress only 0.29, 1.25 line-loss events per run and runs off track. The slalom failure is line loss followed by drift, not oscillation: steering_oscillation there is 0.18 and rms is 0.020 m. The line-loss mechanism is the main problem, and it has three contributors: (1) the 12 mm sensors cover the 25 mm tape only when the robot is within about 18.5 mm of centre, so the sum of readings drops below 0.05 on sharp bends; (2) the robot is at 1.3 base speed on tight bends, which makes the drop-out more likely; (3) mass 0.8 kg and body length 0.16 m give yaw inertia that resists quick turns. Changes: (a) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m, so each sensor keeps seeing tape out to about 20.5 mm off centre and the line is less often lost; the readings also change more smoothly. (b) base_speed 1.3 to 1.2. The oval has time margin (1.97 s against a 3 s limit), so the speed cut mainly helps the slalom and s-bend; a small time cost on those tracks is acceptable because finishing is worth 500 points. (c) mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg and body_length 0.16 to 0.14 m, which lowers yaw inertia (mass*(L^2+W^2)/12) so the robot turns faster into bends and recovers from errors sooner. Kept unchanged: kp 1.5, ki 0, kd 0.6, sensor weights and spread, wheel_track 0.14, wheel_radius 0.03, sensor y 0.05, last_direction line loss, so the effect of the change is easy to read. Expected result: the oval stays at finish rate 1.0; the s-bend finish rate rises above 0.6; the slalom gets its first finishes or at least progress above 0.5 with line_loss_events below 0.5. Hypotheses to test next: (H1) the 16 mm sensors cut line_loss_events on the slalom by more than half; (H2) lower mass and inertia improve the slalom without adding oscillation (steering_oscillation stays below 0.3); (H3) base_speed 1.2 is still fast enough to finish the s-bend in under 3 s, with completion_time near 2.5 s. If the slalom still drifts, the next step is to widen the sensor spread to about plus or minus 3 cm, with the gain rescaled to match.
